svg.title: One agent loop, two wire protocols
svg.desc: The agent loop in backend/main.py makes three calls on a conversation object: add_user_text, next_turn (which returns a Turn of texts and tool calls) and add_tool_results. llm.py implements them twice. OpenAIConversation uses chat completions with function tools: always streamed, tool-call fragments joined by index with missing ids filled in, each tool result its own tool message, and a stream with no chunks reported as a provider fault. AnthropicConversation uses the Messages API with tool use: system prompt and tools are request fields, a turn's results return together as tool_result blocks, invalid arguments mark the result is_error, and a refusal ends the run with a plain message. Both keep an append-only history, flag tool arguments that are not a JSON object, turn provider errors into plain messages, and use a 600 second timeout with 2 SDK retries. NVIDIA NIM (the default) and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint use the first; any Anthropic-compatible endpoint uses the second. settings.py picks the provider from saved Settings, then NEURALFORGE_PROVIDER, then NVIDIA NIM; keys stay in a mode-600 file and are never returned to the browser.
svg.text: One agent loop, two wire protocols
llm.py hides each provider's message format behind three calls, so the loop is the same for every model.
the only three calls the loop makes

text.tspan: Always streamed; some gateways accept nothing else
Tool-call fragments joined by index; missing ids filled in
Each tool result is its own tool message
A stream with no chunks is reported as a provider fault
System prompt and tools are request fields
A turn's results return together, as tool_result blocks
Invalid arguments mark the result is_error
A refusal ends the run with a plain message
Append-only history. Tool arguments that are not a JSON object are flagged on the call, not raised.
Provider errors become plain messages: bad key, no access, not found, rate limit, unreachable. 600 s timeout, 2 SDK retries.

text.tspan: Provider choice: saved Settings, else NEURALFORGE_PROVIDER, else NVIDIA NIM. Saved values win over the environment.
Keys stay in a mode-600 file on this machine and are never returned to the browser. Provider and model are fixed when a run starts.
